page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is a High Frequency Compute virtual server configured with 2 shared vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the hardware features 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. This instance includes 128 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no GPU hardware present.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall within the average range, supported by strong single-threaded gzip compression performance at 32.63 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2405.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 4124.35. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths falling into the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and modest memory footprint position this server as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require dedicated compute resources. The inclusion of fast NVMe storage offsets some memory limitations, though database operations and Redis SET performance remain low. This server is best suited for light web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded utility scripts, and development or testing environments that do not demand sustained multi-core execution.
